met:446060.summary: Cut from a thin piece of mother-of-pearl only 3 cm high and pierced at the top for suspension, this small cross is incised with the figure of the crucified Christ, his arms stretched along the crossbar and his body clothed in a long garment. The simple, lively lines make it a personal devotional pendant, worn by an Egyptian Christian as a sign of faith in the One who died on the cross.
facts: The Met attributes it to Egypt and gives a very broad date range, 3rd–12th century, reflecting how difficult such small devotional objects are to date.
met:446060.notes: Acc. 10.130.1154, Gift of Helen Miller Gould, 1910. The Met date of 3rd–12th century means its placement in the 7th century (y 700) is arbitrary; a crucified Christ wearing a long garment would be consistent with an early date but this is not confirmed. Small incised marks above the figure are not legible in the photograph.
